subtitle: Develop and revise a small paper prototype with people with disabilities and families, guided by their own purposes, the family contributions they choose and a clear account of their influence.
scope: For colleagues developing work with people with disabilities and families in contexts connected with DHS. Six original practice lessons examine a paper question-entry prototype. Neri can choose the paper practice card; no service policy, eligibility, actual assistance arrangement or delegated agency decision is changed. The person’s own contribution and chosen family input remain distinct. Actual applicable accessibility, information, planning and equity responsibilities remain. The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads the program and provides guidance, knowledge and feedback while staff carry their own equity work. Native American and Tribal-specific matters go to the person or area responsible within ADSA (Aging and Disability Services Administration).
introTranscript: Designing with people gives them a part in developing the work, with the actual open choice and decision responsibility clear. Follow a small original paper-card project through a person’s own purpose, chosen family input, personally learned care meanings, three whole alternatives, a performed design choice and exact feedback. Examine how input changes the card rather than count attendance as influence or use a family account in place of the person’s own. You can work through the entire an example or retain a private insight about authorship and shared care without a real service record or public contribution.

lessons.title: Make an open design choice understandable
lessons.summary: Identify what people can shape, who decides and what the original paper exercise cannot change.
lessons.objective: Describe the open paper-card choice and Neri’s responsibility.
objectives: Describe the open paper-card choice and Neri’s responsibility.
Distinguish developing an alternative from approving a predetermined card.
Identify the enlarged authority and influence claims in the whole starting note.
takeaways: Designing together needs an actual question people can help shape.
A clear boundary makes influence understandable rather than imaginary.
Attendance, gratitude and a label do not establish what changed.
lessons.statement: Name the choice people can influence before asking them to help design it.

image.caption: Two people in white coats hold an open book, with one finger pointing to its page.

intro.heading: A paper question card is open to change
intro.body:
A team can invite people into developing alternatives rather than ask for approval after everything is settled. For this course, designing together means working with people to shape a defined piece of work and examining how their contributions affect it. EPA’s public-participation planning guidance distinguishes using input from seeking acceptance of a predetermined outcome. It also makes the actual open questions and decision process important. This is planning guidance, not a new Minnesota procedure or a promise that every agency power can be shared.

Neri is a DHS colleague preparing one paper card for a practice conversation. The entire starting card is: “Choose one of the activities listed below: discussion, presentation or group exercise. Circle the activity and tell the facilitator why it suits you.” Neri has authority in the example to choose the next paper practice card. The choice of its opening question, response space and wording is open. Neri cannot use the exercise to authorize an actual service, change eligibility or promise that a particular assistance method is available.

The original purpose is to help a person express what they want to ask about before choosing a conversation method. That purpose differs from making everyone select an activity first. A participant could help change the card’s first question, propose another entry or explain what an existing form makes difficult. People need not submit a diagnosis or whole history to contribute to this small design question.

The whole starting note reads: “Because people attended, the card was designed together. Their approval gives Neri power over every service arrangement. Any thanks proves the card works for all people with disabilities and families.” Each sentence enlarges the record. Attendance supplies no actual changed design. Approval of a practice card does not confer agency power, and a positive comment cannot establish universal usability or a service outcome.

A clearer initial invitation is: “We are developing a paper card that helps a person state a question before choosing a conversation method. The opening, response space and words are open to change. Neri will choose the next paper card and explain how contributions affected that choice. The exercise makes no actual service or assistance offer.” Privately compare this invitation with the starting note. You may retain an intrinsic insight about honest invitations without recruiting real participants or producing a public design record.

inThisLesson: Read the entire starting card.
Locate the actual open design choice.
Read the whole misleading note and clearer invitation.
Distinguish input, decision responsibility and service authority.
lessons.keyStatement: People can shape the paper card’s opening, response space and words; Neri chooses the next practice card without changing actual services or making attendance proof of influence.

flashcards.back: Working with people to develop a defined paper card, with their contributions and influence explained.
A part of the work that can actually change, rather than a request to endorse a settled result.
Who makes the stated choice and explains how input affected it; the invitation creates no unrelated power.
A specific connection between a contribution and the chosen change, distinct from attendance or thanks.
Assistance the person selects without replacing their own question or requiring family involvement.

items.title: The purpose comes before the activity list
items.body: The original purpose concerns stating a question before choosing a method. The starting card reverses that sequence and may hide an unlisted purpose. An open design inquiry can examine the sequence rather than merely ask which listed activity people like best.

items.title: The next paper card is a genuine small choice
items.body: Neri can change the opening, space and wording in the example. People therefore have something specific to influence. The choice need not encompass every agency power to matter; it should be stated honestly so a paper change is not mistaken for a service arrangement.

items.title: Attendance needs a separate influence account
items.body: A person can attend without seeing their contribution reflected in the work. The later record must show what input was offered and how it affected the choice. A meeting count cannot supply that connection, and gratitude cannot substitute for examining the card.

tabs.label: Ask for approval of the unchanged card
tabs.body: This invitation gives people a reaction role after the activity-first opening has already been fixed. Calling it shared design would conceal the real scope. If only feedback is possible, say so; here Neri actually has room to develop alternatives and should make that room recognizable.

tabs.label: Promise shared control over every service
tabs.body: This invitation sounds expansive but supplies authority the exercise does not confer. It could make a paper-card choice appear to guarantee services or assistance. A useful promise identifies the actual change and decision responsibility instead of widening power through welcoming language.

tabs.label: Invite development of the open paper choice
tabs.body: This invitation names purpose, open parts and Neri’s responsibility. It supports meaningful alternatives and an explanation of influence. People can contribute at a manageable scope while actual service decisions and requirements remain with their relevant roles.

check.question: What makes the initial invitation faithful to this project?
check.correct: It identifies the open paper-card parts, Neri’s choice and a later account of influence while leaving actual service authority distinct.
wrong: It labels attendance as proof the unchanged card was designed together.
It gives every participant power to approve all actual services.
It requires everyone’s diagnosis and complete history before a wording suggestion.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The invitation makes a real small choice understandable without inventing authority or a disclosure condition.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Attendance does not show how the card changed. The invitation confers no actual service powers. A wording suggestion needs no diagnosis or whole history; explain the open choice and decision responsibility instead of enlarging either influence or required disclosure.

sorting.heading: Separate open choice, actual boundary and enlarged claim

items.text: Change the card’s first question.
Revise response space and wording.
Neri chooses the next paper practice card.
The exercise changes no actual eligibility or service offer.
Attendance proves everyone’s input shaped the card.
A positive comment gives Neri every agency decision power.

move.failure: A participation label replaces an explanation of actual influence or authority.

lessons.title: Keep the person’s purpose and chosen family input distinct
lessons.summary: Receive Mina’s own question and Jo’s chosen support contribution without making family participation a substitute for authorship.
lessons.objective: Explain Mina’s own design purpose from the complete account.
objectives: Explain Mina’s own design purpose from the complete account.
Distinguish Jo’s chosen family contribution from decision authority or everyone’s preference.
Identify a card feature that responds to Mina’s purpose without requiring family involvement.
takeaways: People can contribute a purpose without telling their whole history.
Chosen family input can be useful and remain distinct from the person’s account.
Optional support should not become a compulsory entry condition.
lessons.statement: Hear the person’s chosen purpose before interpreting what support should mean.

image.caption: Two people in white coats hold an open book, with one finger pointing to its page.

intro.heading: Two contributions can inform the same card
intro.body:
DHS person-centered-practices discussion connects planning with people’s own purposes rather than allowing existing service options alone to determine the plan. A design exercise can carry that attention into the question it asks first. This does not make every practice card an actual individual support plan. It gives a reason to hear the person’s own purpose and examine whether the proposed entry makes that purpose visible.

Mina is an invented adult with a disability who chooses to contribute to the paper design. Mina’s entire account is: “I want to ask how a question I bring would receive an explanation before I choose a discussion or presentation. The activity list makes me choose a method before I can name that question. I would like room to state my own question, and I do not want my whole history on this card.” The account supplies purpose, sequence and a chosen disclosure limit. It establishes no diagnosis, capacity finding or preference for every disabled person.

Mina chooses to invite Jo, a family member, to add an account of possible help. Jo’s whole contribution is: “Mina asked me to describe how I could help put a chosen question into words if asked. I think a separate place to say what help is wanted could be useful. My contribution does not replace Mina’s question, and Mina may choose to complete the card without me.” No legal-representative status or decision power is supplied. Family relationship and chosen assistance should not be silently converted into either.

Neri can now identify two design contributions. The first is a question entry before an activity choice. The second is an optional place for the person to describe desired help, with the question still their own. Jo adds practical insight; Mina supplies the question’s purpose and boundary. A card that requires a family member would contradict the account, while a card that forbids any chosen help would discard a useful possibility.

Neri’s complete input note is: “Mina wants to name a question before deciding about a conversation method and keep whole-history information off this paper card. Jo proposes an optional place to describe chosen help without replacing Mina’s words or requiring family involvement. These are two particular contributions to the open design question, not everyone’s preferences or actual assistance arrangements.” Privately examine how the note preserves both contributions. You can retain a private insight about authorship and chosen support without obtaining anyone’s real disability or family information.

inThisLesson: Read Mina’s entire account.
Read Jo’s complete chosen contribution.
Distinguish authorship, assistance and authority.
Read the full input note and identify usable features.
lessons.keyStatement: Mina’s question-first purpose and Jo’s help-if-wanted suggestion can both shape the card while Mina’s authorship, disclosure choice and independent entry remain.

items.title: A chosen disclosure limit still allows design input
items.body: Mina names a specific problem with the card’s sequence and requests question space. No whole history is needed to understand that contribution. Respecting the limit keeps the design focused on its purpose instead of making personal disclosure the price of being heard.

items.title: Chosen help can remain under the person’s direction
items.body: Jo describes possible assistance if Mina wants it and explicitly retains completion without Jo. The card can make a place for desired help without presuming family involvement. Useful assistance and personal authorship can coexist rather than become competing claims.

items.title: A family relationship establishes no automatic authority
items.body: Nothing in the account makes Jo a legal representative or gives Jo control over Mina’s words. Neri should retain the supplied role instead of inferring a formal status. Actual planning contexts have their own roles; the practice design does not change them.

tabs.heading: Compare ways to handle the accounts

tabs.label: Replace Mina’s question with Jo’s summary
tabs.body: This response may seem easier but would lose Mina’s own purpose and disclosure boundary. Jo explicitly says the contribution is assistance rather than replacement. A useful design can accept help while keeping the person’s chosen question recognizable.

tabs.label: Exclude all family input to protect independence
tabs.body: This response turns protection into a rule Mina did not choose. Mina invited Jo’s contribution and retained the option to work alone. Independence need not mean rejecting every chosen relationship; preserve both the personal direction and the optional help.

tabs.label: Use the question-first purpose and optional support idea
tabs.body: This response connects each contribution with an actual feature to examine. It avoids family obligation and automatic formal authority. The result can be a better paper prototype without proof that help exists in a service setting or that all people want the same entry.

check.question: Which account preserves both contributions?
check.correct: Mina’s own question-first purpose and disclosure limit guide the card; Jo adds a help-if-wanted idea without replacing authorship or requiring family participation.
wrong: Jo’s family relationship automatically makes Jo the decision-maker for Mina.
A person must disclose a whole history before a question can inform the card.
Protecting authorship requires refusing the family contribution Mina chose to invite.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The account retains Mina’s direction and Jo’s limited practical suggestion without inventing authority or a condition.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Family relationship supplies no automatic decision authority. Mina gives enough design purpose without a whole history. Refusing all chosen family input would erase Mina’s own invitation; preserve personal authorship, optional help and the actual distinct roles.

sorting.heading: Separate personal purpose, chosen contribution and invented condition

items.text: Mina wants question space before a conversation-method choice.
Mina keeps whole-history information off the paper card.
Jo proposes an optional place to describe desired help.
Mina may complete the card without Jo.
Every card must be completed by a family member.
A diagnosis must precede any wording suggestion.

scenario.prompt: What should Neri carry into the alternatives?
options: A compulsory family signature and whole-history field.
The question-first purpose with optional chosen help, preserving Mina’s own authorship and actual roles.
A rule excluding the family contribution Mina invited.
responses: These conditions are absent and would contradict the offered accounts.
This connects both contributions with design features without replacement.
Mina’s chosen invitation matters alongside the option to work alone.

lessons.transfer: Privately connect Mina’s and Jo’s contributions with two possible card features, or retain an authorship insight without real family information.

move.control: You can keep assistance and personal authorship connected but distinct.
move.failure: Family participation becomes automatic authority, compulsory help or forbidden support.
move.next: Privately connect Mina’s and Jo’s contributions with two possible card features, or retain an authorship insight without real family information.

lessons.title: Receive the care meanings behind shared and authored beginnings
lessons.summary: Use a separate conversation to reconsider judgments of dependence and detachment, then revise the whole design invitation.
lessons.objective: Explain Inez’s shared-support and Orin’s first-authorship meanings.
objectives: Explain Inez’s shared-support and Orin’s first-authorship meanings.
Widen Neri’s dependence and detachment judgments through the supplied accounts.
Connect the wider frame with a changed invitation preserving the person’s chosen beginning.
takeaways: Shared support can express recognition of a chosen relationship.
A first personal account can express care for authorship rather than rejection of help.
A wider frame should change the response without classifying families or disabilities.
lessons.statement: Receive what a chosen beginning protects before treating it as a character judgment.

image.caption: Two people in white coats hold an open book, with one finger pointing to its page.

intro.heading: Two personally learned care purposes change the invitation
intro.body:
A separate original voluntary neighborhood recipe-card encounter gives Neri a meaning question. Inez says: “In the chosen cooking circle where I learned to contribute, inviting someone to help describe the shared effort recognized the relationship behind a recipe. I still wanted my chosen part and words to remain mine.” Orin says: “In the chosen story-editing circle where I learned to contribute, speaking the first account myself protected what I meant before anyone helped revise it. I did not mean that all help or relationships had no value.” These are personal accounts of learned care, not family or disability style categories.

Neri initially calls Inez dependent and Orin detached. Those labels make Neri’s familiar form of a good contribution the only meaningful one. Inez’s account explains chosen connection without surrendering authorship. Orin’s explains initial authorship without denying every relationship. The wider frame can receive both purposes and ask how each wants to begin, rather than predict what should matter from family involvement or a desire to speak alone.

The insight changes Neri’s interpretation and proposed words. A design invitation can acknowledge chosen help without making it a prerequisite, and give a person first authorship without requiring isolation. Inez and Orin describe a recipe-card project, so their accounts do not establish Mina’s or Jo’s motives. Mina’s actual question-first purpose and Jo’s actual optional-help contribution retain their own evidence.

Neri’s complete changed recipe-card invitation is: “You can begin with your chosen account and the part you want represented. If you want another person’s help, tell us what help would fit and what should remain in your own words. You can also start alone and decide about help later. We will describe a contributed relationship only as you choose, rather than treat it as dependence or assume a private beginning rejects others.” The four sentences give the wider frame a concrete response: personally directed beginnings and clear contribution limits, rather than a general promise to be nicer.

Council of Europe educational discussion connects personally learned meanings, wider interpretation and contextual response. Neri can understand a care purpose and change an invitation without diagnosing an intercultural orientation or establishing the recipe project’s success. Privately compare the two labels with the whole accounts and changed words. The understanding may matter in its own right; no disability case, family biography, actual recipe contribution or public learning account is required.

Examine dependence and detachment judgments.
Read the whole changed recipe-card invitation.
Keep Mina’s and Jo’s separate design evidence distinct.
lessons.keyStatement: Inez’s chosen connection and Orin’s first-authorship meanings widen Neri’s judgments and change the invitation, without explaining other people’s motives or requiring disclosure.

accordion.heading: Follow the purpose into the response

items.title: Chosen connection can preserve authorship
items.body: Inez names care for a relationship and still retains a chosen part and words. Calling that dependence loses the supplied purpose. An invitation can make help selectable and its contribution clear rather than assume that involvement transfers ownership of the account.

items.title: First authorship can coexist with later help
items.body: Orin wants the first account to convey the intended meaning before revision. The account explicitly does not reject all relationships. Neri can preserve that beginning and leave later help open instead of labeling it detachment or demanding a helper to prove participation.

items.title: Meaning should change more than tone
items.body: The changed invitation offers first account, chosen assistance, later decision and explicit limits on describing relationships. Each feature follows a received purpose. A friendly salutation on an unchanged compulsory-help card would not address the actual misunderstanding.

tabs.label: Make involvement dependence and solitude detachment
tabs.body: This interpretation preserves Neri’s initial labels despite the supplied care purposes. It would make either chosen beginning look deficient. Receive the actual meanings and examine contribution choices instead of making the staff preference the only acceptable one.

tabs.label: Turn the accounts into family or disability rules
tabs.body: This interpretation predicts Mina, Jo or every family from unrelated personal circles. Neither account supports that reach. The meaning encounter can widen Neri’s understanding while the paper design still follows its own actual contributions and choices.

tabs.label: Offer authored beginnings and selected help
tabs.body: This invitation follows both meanings into concrete alternatives for contributing. It keeps words, relationships and possible help under the person’s direction. Acceptance and actual contribution remain unperformed, so the meaningful response change should not be enlarged into project success.

check.question: Which interpretation follows the two complete accounts?
check.correct: Chosen connection and first authorship widen Neri’s labels and inform selectable beginnings, without making either a group rule or replacing Mina’s separate account.
wrong: Inez’s chosen help proves all personal authorship has been surrendered.
Orin’s first account proves every relationship and later help are rejected.
The recipe accounts determine every disabled person’s and family member’s motives.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The interpretation receives each care purpose and follows it into a contextual response with actual scope retained.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Inez expressly keeps a chosen part and words. Orin expressly leaves relationships and help meaningful. Neither personal recipe account explains every disability or family motive; follow the particular purpose into the changed invitation while retaining other people’s own evidence.

sorting.heading: Separate received meaning, changed response and unsupported profile

items.text: Inez’s chosen help recognizes a relationship without surrendering chosen words.
Orin’s first account protects intended meaning before revision.
The invitation offers a first personal account and later help choice.
The invitation describes a relationship only as the contributor chooses.
Every disabled person wants the same family role.
A private beginning proves rejection of all relationships.

options: A permanent family style chart for every future participant.

responses: The individual accounts establish no group chart.

This follows meaning into response without inventing profiles or project results.

lessons.transfer: Privately examine how chosen connection and first authorship protect care, or retain a meaningful insight without a family story or public contribution.

move.control: You can widen a judgment through the person’s supplied care purpose.
move.failure: A chosen beginning becomes a deficit label, group profile or compulsory disclosure.
move.next: Privately examine how chosen connection and first authorship protect care, or retain a meaningful insight without a family story or public contribution.

lessons.title: Develop whole alternatives people can compare
lessons.summary: Compare three complete paper cards by their sequence, authorship and help offered, rather than choosing the friendliest title.
lessons.objective: Compare the actual text of cards A, B and C.
objectives: Compare the actual text of cards A, B and C.
Connect Mina’s and Jo’s contributions with specific design features.
Distinguish a reasoned paper comparison from proof of actual service access.
takeaways: Whole alternatives make consequences easier to inspect.
A design feature should have a reason connected with the offered input.
Different cards can address one purpose without a universal best-method claim.
lessons.statement: Put the actual alternatives beside the contributions they are meant to serve.

image.caption: Two people in white coats hold an open book, with one finger pointing to its page.

intro.heading: Three cards ask people to begin differently
intro.body:
The open purpose is to help a person state a question before choosing a conversation method. Mina wants a first question and no whole-history requirement. Jo proposes an optional place for chosen help while Mina retains authorship and may work alone. Neri develops three entire alternatives so participants can compare actual words and sequence, rather than rely on labels such as simple, independent or collaborative.

Card A reads: “Choose one of these activities: discussion, presentation or group exercise. Circle the activity and tell the facilitator why it suits you.” It preserves the activity-first sequence. It may help someone whose question and preferred method are already known, but it does not address Mina’s stated beginning. Calling this card simple cannot make an unlisted question appear or show where desired help can be described.

Card B reads: “What would you like to ask about? Write your question in the space below. We will discuss a conversation method after the question is clear.” This card changes the sequence and offers authored question space. It responds to Mina’s purpose. It says nothing about Jo’s optional-help idea; absence of a place for that idea does not prove Neri hostile or that actual help is impossible, but it identifies a design difference worth examining.

Card C reads: “What would you like to ask about? Write your question in the space below. Help with words, if wanted: write what help you want in a separate space. We will discuss a conversation method after the question is clear.” This adds a separate help space without requiring a family member or replacing the first question. The wording remains a paper prototype rather than an actual assistance offer. Participants can examine whether the help space is clearly optional and whether a blank would be misunderstood.

Neri’s entire comparison is: “A begins with a listed activity and does not address the offered question-first purpose. B puts the question first but leaves the optional-help contribution unrepresented. C puts the question first and creates a separate place for chosen help, with the help wording still needing review. I favor examining C further for this paper purpose, without treating it as the best card for every person or proof of an available service.” The account connects input, feature and remaining question. Privately compare the three cards or retain an intrinsic insight about what an apparently simple beginning leaves out; no actual service participant or survey is required.

inThisLesson: Read every word of the three alternatives.
Compare activity-first and question-first sequence.
Examine the separate optional-help space.
Read the full reasoned comparison and its remaining question.
lessons.keyStatement: C represents both the offered question-first and optional-help ideas, while the help wording still needs review; this is a specific paper comparison rather than a universal access finding.

items.title: A keeps the familiar activity sequence
items.body: A may seem easy because its choices are already listed. For Mina’s purpose, however, it asks for a method before making the question visible. Naming the actual sequence is more useful than praise or blame because it shows which offered design problem remains unanswered.

items.title: B makes room for the question but not the help idea
items.body: B changes the first task and keeps the question authored by the person. That is a concrete contribution. It does not represent the separate optional-help suggestion, so a comparison should retain the gain and the missing feature rather than call the card wholly successful or wholly uncaring.

items.title: C connects two contributions but needs another reading
items.body: C gives question and desired help separate spaces. This preserves authorship better than a compulsory helper field, yet optionality and interpretation of blanks still deserve attention. Selecting it for a paper review is a reasoned next step, not proof everyone can use it or that assistance has been arranged.

tabs.heading: Compare ways to choose the next card

tabs.label: Choose A because a short list looks simple
tabs.body: This choice treats familiar appearance as evidence that Mina’s purpose has been met. The whole text still begins with a method. A good comparison examines what the person is asked to do and why, rather than assuming a short list is always the most usable entry.

tabs.label: Choose B and declare help irrelevant
tabs.body: B genuinely represents the first-question contribution, but that does not make Jo’s chosen idea irrelevant. The two accounts can coexist. Naming a feature B lacks makes the next discussion precise without blaming Neri or manufacturing an actual help entitlement.

tabs.label: Review C for its question and separate help spaces
tabs.body: This choice connects both actual contributions with particular words and asks what still needs improvement. The alternatives remain inspectable, including their tradeoffs. The paper purpose and participant evidence guide this review rather than a ranking of people or a promise of universal suitability.

check.question: Why does Neri propose another reading of C?
check.correct: C represents the first-question and separate-help ideas, but the optional-help wording and interpretation of blanks still need examination for this paper purpose.
wrong: C guarantees every actual service and assistance arrangement will be accessible.
A has met Mina’s question-first purpose because the list is short.
B’s first question proves every chosen help contribution is irrelevant.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. Neri gives a specific reason linked to both inputs and retains an actual design question for the next round.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A paper feature guarantees no actual service access. A short list still asks Mina to choose a method first. B’s question-first gain does not erase Jo’s separate help idea; compare the full words and their consequences rather than enlarge appearance or one useful feature into a universal result.

sorting.heading: Separate card feature, offered input and enlarged conclusion

items.text: A begins with discussion, presentation or group exercise.
C adds a separate help-with-words space.
Mina wants to name the question before a method.
Jo suggests optional help without replacing Mina’s words.
The card proves every actual assistance method is available.
A short list proves the question-first purpose has been met.

move.control: You can connect an actual feature with a particular contribution and consequence.
move.failure: A title, short list or useful feature becomes proof of universal fit.
move.next: Privately compare one feature and one remaining question in the full cards, or retain an intrinsic insight about beginnings without a real service review.

lessons.summary: Follow exact feedback into a selected and revised card, retaining input, reasons and decision responsibility.
lessons.objective: Identify Mina’s and Jo’s exact reactions to card C.
objectives: Identify Mina’s and Jo’s exact reactions to card C.
Explain the link between Mina’s blank-space concern and the added wording.
Distinguish Neri’s performed paper choice from actual service authorization or unanimous agreement.
takeaways: A second round can change a specific feature rather than repeat the same invitation.
Decision reasons should show how input affected the work.
A small performed choice matters without becoming universal consensus or service authority.
lessons.statement: Show the contribution, the change and the reason together.

image.caption: Two people in white coats hold an open book, with one finger pointing to its page.

intro.heading: An optional space gains an explicit explanation
intro.body:
Neri performs a paper-reading exchange in the example by presenting C’s entire text from the previous lesson and asking: “Does the opening make your question visible, and what might the separate help space mean?” The question keeps the remaining design issue open. It does not ask Mina or Jo to certify every arrangement or represent everyone with a disability or family connection.

Mina’s full reply is: “The first question is the change I asked for. I want the help space to be optional, and a blank should not be read as refusing every kind of help. I am commenting on the words, not trying the card in a service conversation.” Jo’s full reply is: “The separate space lets desired help be named without replacing Mina’s question. Please say a family member is not required. I am not making the question or decision for Mina.” The comments identify gains and two wording questions; neither supplies actual card use, every family preference or unanimous approval of all design features.

Neri chooses and writes this whole revised paper card: “What would you like to ask about? Write your question in the space below. Help with words, if wanted: describe the help you want in a separate space. You can leave this help space blank; a blank is not a statement that no help is wanted, and a family member is not required. We will discuss a conversation method after the question is clear.” The revised fourth sentence connects Mina’s blank concern and Jo’s family-condition concern with actual words. The first question and separate help space retain the original two contributions.

Neri’s entire choice note is: “I selected revised C for this paper practice because it puts the person’s question first and gives chosen help a separate place. Mina’s concern changed the wording about optional space and blanks. Jo’s concern added the sentence that family involvement is not required. This is my stated paper-card choice, not agreement from every participant, an actual service offer or proof of use.” There is now a performed design choice and an explanation of influence, rather than only planned consultation. The record should recognize that concrete output without inventing what happened after it.

Actual staff work remains governed by its relevant responsibilities. DHS Equity Policy describes daily equity consideration and qualifying formal analysis or scan toolkit requirements, including its custom-tool consultation provision. A paper exercise replaces none of those requirements and gives Neri no service power. The consultant leads the program and provides guidance while staff carry their work. Privately follow one contribution through the chosen words and reason, or retain a private insight about taking an offered concern seriously; no real project approval or public participation account is necessary.

accordion.heading: Keep influence attached to a specific change

items.title: Mina’s concern changes the meaning of a blank
items.body: The revised fourth sentence says the help space is optional and a blank is not a refusal of every kind of help. This directly addresses Mina’s concern. It avoids treating missing entry as a firm preference, while making no claim that help is already available or that Mina has tried the card.

items.title: Jo’s concern removes a family condition
items.body: The new wording expressly says a family member is not required. Jo’s suggested help still has a place, with Mina’s first question retained. The change recognizes the chosen contribution without making Jo the author, decision-maker or representative of every family.

items.title: Neri’s choice has a stated reason and limit
items.body: Neri actually chooses the revised paper card within the example. The note connects both concerns with words and retains the stated purpose. It is appropriate to recognize this influence and output without calling it unanimous agreement, adopted service policy or actual use.

tabs.label: Count two replies and stop there
tabs.body: Two replies show input was supplied, but the count alone does not describe its effect. Mina’s blank concern and Jo’s family-condition concern change specific text. A useful account connects each comment with the feature rather than making participation volume the whole result.

tabs.label: Call the paper choice everyone’s service decision
tabs.body: This account moves beyond Neri’s stated authority and the comments’ scope. Neither person has agreed on every service or tried the card. The performed choice is meaningful as a paper design output, with actual service responsibilities and remaining practical questions distinct.

tabs.label: Describe the changed text and Neri’s reasons
tabs.body: This account makes actual influence inspectable. It retains the question-first gain, separate-help space and two new clarifications. It also records who chose the paper version, avoiding both an empty participation label and a manufactured unanimous or operational result.

check.question: What does the performed round establish?
check.correct: Two exact comments changed the revised fourth sentence, and Neri selected that paper version with reasons; actual use, universal agreement and service arrangements remain unestablished.
wrong: Two replies alone prove everyone’s perspective was represented.
Neri’s paper choice authorizes every requested actual service.
A blank help field proves the person refuses every possible kind of help.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The account follows specific influence and a performed small choice while retaining their actual scope.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Two replies supply two particular perspectives, not everyone’s. A paper choice confers no service authority. The explicit revision avoids reading a blank as refusing all help; recognize the actual linked changes without enlarging representation, power or missing information.

lessons.title: Close with influence, choice and the next honest question
lessons.summary: Recognize the actual revised design and particular comments while leaving use, wider fit and service arrangements open.
lessons.objective: Describe what Mina’s and Jo’s complete closing comments support.
objectives: Describe what Mina’s and Jo’s complete closing comments support.
Distinguish the performed paper change from untested actual use and wider fit.
Retain a practical continuation or intrinsic private care insight without claiming permanent competence.
takeaways: A changed design and explained influence are concrete gains.
Commenting on words is different from trying an actual arrangement.
Private understanding can remain worthwhile alongside unfinished work.
lessons.statement: Recognize what people changed without making their comments say more than they do.

image.caption: Two people in white coats hold an open book, with one finger pointing to its page.

intro.heading: The paper choice is real in the example; service use is not
intro.body:
Mina’s whole closing comment is: “I can point to the first question and to the sentence about blanks as changes connected with my contribution. I have not used this card in an actual service conversation. I still want any later method choice to follow the question I choose to ask.” Jo’s whole closing comment is: “The card keeps chosen help separate and says a family member is not required. That addresses my contribution without making me Mina’s author or decision-maker. I have not tested whether the card fits other people or actual arrangements.” These comments are specific rather than blanket praise.

Neri’s complete closing account is: “Mina’s question-first contribution and Jo’s help-if-wanted idea shaped the alternatives. Their next comments changed the wording about blanks and family involvement. I selected the revised paper card and explained both links. The closing comments recognize those particular changes, with actual use, wider fit and service arrangements still open.” The whole four-sentence account gives the claim of shared design substance: people influenced alternatives and a revision within the stated scope, and the decision responsibility remained visible.

A relevant continuation, if an actual authorized project follows, would examine the card’s use with its intended purpose, access arrangements, information limits and actual decision responsibilities. No such project or trial is supplied here. The missing trial should limit claims of usability or service improvement, not erase the performed paper output and the participants’ recognized influence. Likewise, the two comments do not represent all disabled people, all families or all possible preferences.

Inez’s chosen-connection and Orin’s first-authorship meanings provide another learning gain. They widened Neri’s dependence and detachment labels and changed a whole recipe-card invitation. The invitation has not been accepted, and the encounter predicts none of Mina’s or Jo’s motives. You can still retain a personal insight about receiving chosen support and authored beginnings without a service result, biography or public reflection. Personal understanding and a practical output have distinct value and evidence.

Designing together is more credible when its open choice, contributions, changed work and decision reasons remain visible. A welcoming label alone is insufficient, while an accurately limited small choice need not be dismissed for failing to change everything. Privately name one actual influence link and one unanswered question from the full example, or keep a care insight for your own understanding. Staff responsibility and consultant program leadership continue; completion certifies no permanent skill or group result.

lessons.keyStatement: The alternatives, revised sentence and explained choice support actual paper-design influence, with actual use and wider fit open; the separate care insight can remain privately meaningful.

items.title: Mina can identify particular influence
items.body: The first question and blank explanation connect with Mina’s offered concerns. The comment recognizes those links while expressly retaining no actual use. A faithful closing can acknowledge influence without interpreting it as every person’s satisfaction or a completed service result.

items.title: Jo recognizes a contribution without replacing authorship
items.body: The optional help space and no-family condition address Jo’s chosen input. Jo retains Mina’s own question and decision position. The closing should describe that contribution rather than turn the family account into automatic formal authority or evidence of wider fit.

items.title: A private care insight needs no public performance
items.body: The separate recipe encounter changes Neri’s interpretation and proposed words. Its scope is personal understanding rather than an actual service outcome. The insight can be retained privately without denial of its value or a manufactured competence label.

tabs.label: Declare the card works for everyone
tabs.body: This interpretation turns two wording comments into universal usability and actual access results. Both accounts retain explicit limits. Their influence can be recognized more credibly by naming the particular paper changes and the actual questions that remain.

tabs.label: Deny all influence because no service trial followed
tabs.body: This interpretation loses the full alternatives, performed revision, Neri’s choice and the recognized comment-to-word links. An unperformed service trial matters for operational claims, but it does not erase the paper design influence. Keep the different levels of evidence distinct.

tabs.label: Recognize paper influence and a fitting continuation
tabs.body: This interpretation follows the entire record rather than a participation count or universal success claim. It names the two rounds, changed work and decision reasons while leaving actual use and fit open. It also allows personal understanding without a real project or public learning account.

check.question: Which closing account fits all supplied evidence?
check.correct: The two rounds shaped a selected paper revision with explained influence; actual use, wider fit and service results remain open, and the separate care insight can remain private.
wrong: The closing comments guarantee every person and family can use every service.
No service trial means the performed paper changes and input links never happened.
Private understanding matters only if a biography, actual outcome and public report follow.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The account recognizes actual design influence and its limit without enlarging the outcome or requiring public proof of growth.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Particular wording comments cannot guarantee all service access. Absence of a trial does not undo the performed paper choice and linked revision. Private care understanding can matter without a biography, operational outcome or public report; retain its scope alongside actual unfinished work.

sorting.heading: Separate supported gain, open question and enlarged conclusion

items.text: Two comments changed the selected paper card’s fourth sentence.
Mina and Jo recognize specific links with their contributions.
Actual use and wider fit remain untested.
Actual service and assistance arrangements remain separate.
Two comments prove every family’s view is represented.
Private care learning is invalid without a public biography.

jobAid.title: Develop a paper choice with people’s contributions
jobAid.subtitle: An original shared-design comparison and reflection aid; actual services, accessibility, planning, information and formal equity responsibilities remain distinct.
remember: Name the open choice and decision responsibility. Receive the person’s own purpose and chosen family input, develop whole alternatives, show how comments changed the work and distinguish the paper result from actual use.

sections.heading: Start with an honest open choice
items: Neri can choose the paper practice card’s opening, response space and words. The purpose is to state a question before choosing a conversation method; actual service authority does not change.

The starting note wrongly treats attendance as influence, approval as agency power and thanks as universal usability. The whole initial invitation names actual open parts and a later explanation of influence.

sections.heading: Receive authorship and chosen help
items: Mina wants a question-first entry and no whole-history requirement. Jo offers an optional help idea at Mina’s invitation, without replacing the question or requiring family involvement.
Family relationship establishes no automatic formal authority. Keep the actual contribution and the person’s own direction distinct rather than require or forbid chosen help.

sections.heading: Receive personally learned care purposes
items: Inez connects chosen recipe help with recognizing a relationship while retaining own words; Orin connects a first account with intended authorship before revision. They widen Neri’s dependence and detachment labels.

The changed whole recipe invitation offers an authored beginning, selected help and later choice. The accounts predict neither Mina’s nor Jo’s motives or disability/family styles; private understanding remains worthwhile.

sections.heading: Compare actual alternatives
items: A begins with listed activities. B begins with the person’s question. C begins with the question and adds a separate desired-help space. Read the full words rather than choose a friendly label or short list.
C represents both actual contributions but still needs clarity about optionality and blanks. A paper comparison establishes no actual assistance arrangement or universal usability.

sections.heading: Make influence visible
items: Mina’s next comment asks that a blank not mean refusing every kind of help. Jo asks that family involvement not be required. Neri selects revised C and adds both clarifications to its fourth sentence.

The complete choice note connects input, changed words and Neri’s responsibility. Actual daily staff equity work and qualifying formal DHS analysis or scan toolkit/custom-tool consultation requirements remain; the consultant leads the program and provides guidance while staff carry their work.

sections.heading: Close with gains and open questions
items: Mina and Jo recognize specific input-to-wording links while retaining no actual use or wider-fit test. Neri’s whole closing describes two rounds and a performed paper revision rather than universal agreement or service success.

A relevant actual continuation needs its purpose, access and information arrangements and actual decision responsibilities. Private care understanding remains valuable without a public biography or service result. Native American and Tribal-specific matters go to the person or area responsible within ADSA (Aging and Disability Services Administration).

sources.note: Connects work with people’s own purposes rather than available options alone. The paper design preserves personal direction and chosen help without becoming an actual support plan or service decision.

sources.title: Council of Europe — Developing intercultural competence through education
sources.note: Supports receiving personally learned care meanings, widening interpretation and changing a contextual response. The original recipe encounter describes particular people rather than family or disability styles; intrinsic private understanding remains worthwhile.
